# Best portable power stations for a CPAP

**My top pick is the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2.** It has 1,024 Wh of capacity, a 10 ms UPS switchover, and a quiet rating of about 20 dB. It recharges in about 49 minutes and weighs 24.9 lb. It costs about $700. ([Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/), [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/))

## Other good options

| Need | Pick | Capacity / price | Runtime (8-hr nights) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Home backup that can grow | EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus | 1,024 Wh, expandable to 5 kWh, about $719 | ~2.7 humidifier off, ~1.2-1.7 on |
| Cheaper 1 kWh | Bluetti Elite 100 V2 | 1,024 Wh, $499 | ~2.7 off, ~1.2 on |
| Small and cheap | EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus | 286 Wh, 10.4 lb, ~$279-299 | ~0.8 off, ~0.3-0.5 on |
| Lowest-cost CPAP-only | Tenergy T320 | 300 Wh, pure sine confirmed, $225.99 | About one night, humidifier off |

- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2:** the BuyerSheet table has "Check on Amazon" and official-store buttons for it: [BuyerSheet](https://www.buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/cpap/).
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus:** it has the same capacity and UPS speed as the Anker. Its main advantage is expandability. It is also heavier at 27.6 lb. [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/23/best-power-station-for-cpap/) has the details. [PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap) lists the standard DELTA 3 at $599 with an Amazon link.
- **Bluetti Elite 100 V2:** [buy on Amazon via PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap)
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus:** it only covers one night if you skip the humidifier. Both RIVER 3 Plus sources I found disagree on its runtime, and I trust the math over the "multi-night" claim in [Outage Power Guide](https://outagepowerguide.com/reviews/best-power-station-for-cpap-machines/).
- **Tenergy T320:** [buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-t320-300wh-power-station) (affiliate link). Recharging takes about 8 hours, and it's the only unit in that source's records with confirmed pure sine output ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-portable-power-station-for-cpap-machine-2026-runtime-humidifier-pure-sine-w)).

## Choosing

- **Humidifier use:** a heated humidifier roughly doubles power draw. Sources estimate 320 Wh per night without it and 520-720 Wh with it. If you use one, get 1 kWh or more.
- **Sizing:** nightly Wh × nights ÷ 0.85. For two humidified nights at 520 Wh, you need about 1,220 Wh.
- **DC cord:** running your CPAP from the station's 12V port with the maker's approved DC cord typically adds 10-20% runtime. Don't use a generic car adapter.
- **Pure sine wave:** this is required. Most current units have it, but check the spec sheet.
- **UPS switchover:** if you want the station to take over automatically in an outage while you sleep, look for around 10 ms.

## Caveats

- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2:** it is light and popular ($499, [Jackery listing via PowerStationBench](https://powerstationbench.com/best/power-station-for-cpap)). However, Jackery says its stations aren't recommended for medical devices, and its switchover is up to 20 ms. I'd pick another brand if you depend on your CPAP.
- **Testing:** the Tested Watts picks are based on spec sheets and calculations, not hands-on testing.
- **Prices:** they move often, so check the retailer before buying.
- **Your CPAP maker:** ask them and your provider about backup power.

If you tell me your CPAP model, whether you use the humidifier, and how many nights of backup you want, I can narrow this to one pick.
